Explain how the structure of DNA relates to its function as the molecule of heredity. Refer to base pairing, strand directionality, and the semiconservative model of replication.

Primer.back: A short nucleic acid strand that gives DNA polymerase a free 3′ end to extend. In replication it is RNA (10 to 12 nucleotides in E. coli), made by primase. In PCR it is a synthetic DNA oligonucleotide of about 20 nucleotides.

DNA ligase.back: Seals nicks in the DNA backbone by forming phosphodiester bonds. It joins Okazaki fragments in replication, and joins an insert to a vector in cloning.

What's the formula for calculating cells.back: Cells per mL = colonies counted × 10^|dilution| × 10. The final × 10 is because 100 µL (0.1 mL) was spread on the plate.

What isotopes did Hershey and Chase use,.back: ³²P labels DNA (phosphorus is in the DNA backbone, not protein). ³⁵S labels protein (sulfur is in cysteine and methionine, not DNA). After infection and blending, ³²P was inside the bacteria in the pellet and passed to progeny phage; ³⁵S stayed outside with the empty phage coats. So DNA is what enters the cell and carries the genetic information.
